name: olostep-mcp

tools.name: create_map
tools.description: Use this when you need the list of URLs on a website, not their content: to see a site's pages, find a section, or pick pages to scrape. Can rank URLs by `search_query` and filter them with glob patterns. Returns URLs only. To get the content of many pages from the site, use create_crawl.

url.description: Website URL to extract links from.

search_query.description: Optional search query to filter URLs (e.g., "blog").

top_n.description: Optional limit for number of URLs returned.

tools.name: create_crawl
tools.description: Use this when you need the content of many pages from one website, such as a docs section or a blog: it follows links from a start URL and scrapes each page it finds, up to `max_pages`. Waits up to `wait_for_completion_seconds` (default 45) and returns the pages if the crawl finishes in that time; otherwise returns a crawl_id to pass to get_crawl_results (not get_batch_results). For a known list of URLs use batch_scrape_urls; for one page use scrape_website.

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl. Set to 1 to scrape only the start URL.

country.description: Optional country code for location-specific crawling.

parser.description: Optional parser ID for specialized content extraction.

wait_for_completion_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the crawl to finish and return its pages in this call. 0 returns the crawl_id right away.

tools.name: get_crawl_results
tools.description: Use this to get the pages of a crawl started with create_crawl, using its crawl_id. While the crawl is in_progress it returns the status: call again in about 10 seconds. Once completed it returns each page's url, title and content, up to `items_limit` per call; when `has_more` is true, pass `next_cursor` for the rest. Do not start a new crawl to check on one that is still running.

crawl_id.description: The crawl_id (or id) returned from create_crawl.

formats.description: Content formats to retrieve per page. Default: ["markdown"].

items_limit.description: Max number of pages to retrieve content for (1-100). Default: 20.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for list-pages. Default: 0 (first page).

search_query.description: Optional filter to rank/select pages by relevance to a query.

max_characters.description: Max characters of content per page (default 20000). Longer pages are cut and link to their full text.

tools.name: batch_scrape_urls
tools.description: Use this when you have a known list of URLs to scrape, such as URLs from a CSV or from search results (up to 100k in one batch). Waits up to `wait_for_completion_seconds` (default 45) and returns the content if the batch finishes in that time. Larger batches usually take 5-8 min and return a batch_id: get their content with get_batch_results, a set at a time, passing `next_cursor` for the rest. For one or a few URLs, scrape_website is faster; to discover a site's pages, use create_crawl.

urls.description: Array of URLs to scrape — plain URL strings, or objects with "url" and optional "custom_id".

output_format.description: Choose format for all URLs. Default: "markdown".

country.description: Optional country code for location-specific scraping.

wait_before_scraping.description: Wait time in milliseconds before scraping each URL.

parser.description: Optional parser ID for specialized extraction (e.g. @olostep/google-search).

wait_for_completion_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the batch to finish and return its content in this call. 0 returns the batch_id right away.

tools.name: get_batch_results
tools.description: Use this to get the content of a batch started with batch_scrape_urls, using its batch_id. While the batch is in_progress it returns the status: call again in about 10 seconds. Once completed it returns each URL's url, title and content, up to `items_limit` per call; when `has_more` is true, pass `next_cursor` for the rest. Do not start a new batch to check on one that is still running.

batch_id.description: The batch_id (or id) returned from batch_scrape_urls.

formats.description: Content formats to retrieve per URL. Default: ["markdown"].

items_limit.description: Max number of items to retrieve content for per call (1-100). Default: 20.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Pass next_cursor from the previous result to get the next pages. Default: 0 (first page).

max_characters.description: Max characters of content per URL (default 20000). Longer pages are cut and link to their full text.

tools.name: answers
tools.description: Use this when the user asks a factual question the live web can answer in a sentence or a few fields, such as a company's founding year, a CEO's name or a product's current price. Searches and reads the pages itself and returns the answer with its source URLs, optionally as a flat JSON object of the fields you list in `json`. For a list of items from one page (latest blog posts, a price table), call scrape_website on that page instead.

task.description: Question or task to answer using web data.

json.description: Optional shape for the answer: a flat JSON object of the fields you want. Example: { "book_title": "", "author": "", "release_date": "" }. Keep it flat. Deeply nested shapes or long lists are unreliable.

tools.name: search_web
tools.description: Use this when you need web pages on a topic and do not have a URL yet. Returns up to `limit` results (1-25), each with its URL, title and description. Set scrape_results to true to also get each result page's content as markdown in the same call (each scraped page costs extra credits); otherwise pass the URLs you need to scrape_website, or to batch_scrape_urls for many. Use include_domains to search one site. For a direct factual answer with sources, use answers.

limit.description: Number of results to return, from 1 to 25. Default: 10.

include_domains.description: Only return results from these domains, e.g. ["docs.olostep.com"].

exclude_domains.description: Never return results from these domains.

scrape_results.description: Also scrape each result and return its content as markdown. Each scraped page uses extra credits.

max_characters.description: With scrape_results, the maximum characters of content returned per page. Default: 20000.

tools.name: scrape_website
tools.description: Use this when you have a URL and need what is on the page. Returns the page as clean markdown (default), html or text, with its url and title, after rendering JavaScript. For structured fields, set output_format to "json" with an llm_extract schema or a parser. Long pages are cut at max_characters (default 20,000) with a link to the full text. For many known URLs use batch_scrape_urls; for many pages of one site use create_crawl.

url.description: The URL of the website you want to scrape.

output_format.description: Output format. "markdown" (default), "html", and "text" need no extra config. "json" returns STRUCTURED data and requires either a `parser` OR an `llm_extract` schema describing the fields to pull. Do not request "json" on its own.

country.description: Optional country code (e.g., US, GB, CA) for location-specific scraping.

wait_before_scraping.description: Wait time in milliseconds before scraping (0-10000). Useful for dynamic content.

parser.description: Optional parser ID for specialized extraction (e.g., "@olostep/amazon-it-product").

llm_extract.description: Defines what to pull when output_format is "json". Provide a `schema` (a JSON-schema object of the fields you want, e.g. { "type": "object", "properties": { "title": { "type": "string" } } }) and/or a `prompt`. Required for JSON output unless a `parser` is given.

max_characters.description: Max characters of page content to return (default 20000). Longer pages are cut and link to their full text; raise this to read more.

instructions:
Olostep gives you live web data. Pick the tool by goal:
- Find pages on a topic, no URL yet: search_web.
- Read one known URL: scrape_website.
- A factual answer with sources: answers.
- List a site's URLs without their content: create_map.
- Content of many pages from one site: create_crawl.
- Content of a known list of URLs: batch_scrape_urls.

create_crawl and batch_scrape_urls return the content if the job finishes within wait_for_completion_seconds; otherwise they return a crawl_id or batch_id. Fetch it with get_crawl_results or get_batch_results, and do not start a new job for the same URLs.
Page content is cut at 20,000 characters per page by default. A cut page says so and links to its full text; call scrape_website with a higher max_characters to read more.
For structured fields from a page, call scrape_website with output_format "json" and an llm_extract schema.
For a list of items on one page (latest posts, a price table), scrape that page rather than using answers.
